stem.text: Write \( \int_{1}^{7} 3t^{2}\,dt \) as the limit of a right Riemann sum with n subintervals of equal width, using k as the index of summation.

worked_solution.text: The interval [1, 7] has length 6, so each of the n subintervals has width \( \Delta t = \frac{6}{n} \).
The right endpoint of the kth subinterval is \( t_k = 1 + \frac{6k}{n} \), for k = 1 to n.
Multiply the function value at each right endpoint by the width and take the limit: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 3\left(1 + \frac{6k}{n}\right)^{2} \cdot \frac{6}{n} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums

options.label: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 3\left(\frac{6k}{n}\right)^{2} \cdot \frac{6}{n} \)
options.derivation: the sample points started at 0 instead of 1, so the sum is over [0, 6], an interval the integral never gives

options.label: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 3\left(1 + \frac{6k}{n}\right)^{2} \cdot \frac{1}{n} \)
options.derivation: the width taken as 1/n as though the interval had length 1, although the sample points step by 6/n

options.label: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 3\left(1 + \frac{6k}{n}\right)^{2} \)
options.derivation: the function values at the right endpoints added with no subinterval width
